endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS) per BICR, analyzed in the ITT-PFS population (first 480 randomized subjects).

citations.quote: ITT-PFS: The first 480 subjects randomized (320 in the tucatinib arm; 160 in the control arm). This population was used to analyze the primary endpoint of PFS per BICR.

n.text: 612 randomized (410 tucatinib arm, 202 control arm); primary PFS analyzed in first 480.

citations.quote: ITT-OS: All randomized subjects (N=612; 410 in the tucatinib arm, 202 in the control arm). This population was used to analyze the key secondary endpoints of OS
ITT-PFS: The first 480 subjects randomized (320 in the tucatinib arm; 160 in the control arm). This population was used to analyze the primary endpoint of PFS per BICR.
Median PFS by BICR was 7.8 months (95% CI: 7.5, 9.6) in the tucatinib arm compared to 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.2, 7.1) in the control arm (HR 0.54, 95% CI: 0.42, 0.71, p<0.00001).
Median OS was 21.9 months (95% CI: 18.3, 31.0) in the tucatinib arm compared to 17.4 months (95% CI: 13.6, 19.9) in the control arm (HR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.50, 0.87, p=0.00480).
In patients with measurable disease, ORR was 40.6% (95% CI: 35.3, 46.0) in the tucatinib arm compared to 22.8% (95% CI: 16.7, 29.8) in the control arm (p=0.00008).

indication.text: TUKYSA in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine for treatment of adult patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, who have received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting.

citations.quote: TUKYSA is indicated in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine for treatment of adult patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases, who have received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting.

target_moa.text: Tucatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor of HER2; in vitro it inhibits phosphorylation of HER2 and HER3, inhibiting downstream MAPK and AKT signaling and cell proliferation, with reduced potency for related kinases (28- to 88-fold more potent for HER2 than EGFR).

citations.quote: Tucatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor of HER2. In vitro, tucatinib inhibits phosphorylation of HER2 and HER3, resulting in inhibition of downstream MAPK and AKT signaling and cell proliferation, and showed anti-tumor activity in HER2 expressing tumor cells.
Based on Ki calculations, tucatinib has a 28- to 88-fold increase in potency for HER2 relative to EGFR and a 92 to 105-fold increase in potency for HER2 relative to HER4.
Tucatinib is an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor of HER2. It does not have approval for any indication worldwide.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nausea, fatigue, hepatotoxicity, vomiting, stomatitis. Diarrhea occurred in 81% (12% Grade 3, 0.5% Grade 4). Serious adverse reactions in 26%; fatal adverse reactions in 2%; discontinuation for AEs in 6%.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) are diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nausea, fatigue, hepatotoxicity, vomiting, stomatitis, decreased appetite, abdominal pain, headache, anemia, and rash. (6.1)
In HER2CLIMB, 81% of patients who received TUKYSA experienced diarrhea, including 12% with Grade 3 diarrhea and 0.5% with Grade 4 diarrhea.
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 26% of patients who received TUKYSA.
Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2% of patients who received TUKYSA including sudden death, sepsis, dehydration, and cardiogenic shock.
Adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in 6% of patients who received TUKYSA.
